dispatch.decode: recurrent, cached conv window + recurrent state (§04b.1)
dispatch.solve_branch: triangular (A-16: the substitution branch is a different number and is not what was pinned)
dispatch.reference_impl: the installed torch fallbacks; which function objects ran is recorded per block under agreement_at_write_time

input.method: speccheck/moe_ref.py §Input generation via gdn_ref.gdn_input: fp32 torch.randn from a private torch.Generator('cpu').manual_seed(seed), each row rescaled to RMS exactly 1.0, cast to bf16. [ASSUMPTION A-01] RMS-1 models a layernorm output; it does NOT carry the (1+weight) modulation of a real activation

same_input_as_the_moe_dump.reading: byte-identical because both are speccheck/moe_ref.py make_input over the same seed and row count; the GDN dump draws tokens+k_conv-1 rows and slices the first `tokens` of the same generator stream
same_input_as_the_moe_dump.caveat: [ASSUMPTION A-01] neither is a real activation: the MoE dump models post_attention_layernorm output and this one models input_layernorm output (file 03 §03.3), and both are RMS-1 without the (1+w) modulation. Same fixture, not the same layer of a real pass.

reading_rules.payload: raw little-endian element bytes, no header; bytes == elements x itemsize, and `--verify` refuses a record whose size cannot hold its own declared shape (pitfalls/30 §read a dump's dtype off its file size)
reading_rules.bf16: two bytes per element, bit image — read with a uint16 view then bitcast, never cast the uint16 to a float (pitfalls/30 §Tensor.to casts, .view bitcasts)
reading_rules.orientations: conv_pre/conv_out/conv_window are [B, conv_dim, T] (the conv's own orientation, §04.3); q_pre/k_pre/v_pre are [B,T,h,d]; q_hat/k_hat/scan_out are [B,h_v,T,d] in the scan dtype; core_attn/normed are [B,T,h_v,d_v] in the activation dtype; state is [B,h_v,d_k,d_v] F32
reading_rules.scan_out_vs_core_attn: the same values, transposed and cast — pinning only core_attn would hide an exit-cast bug (pitfalls/30 §a hook that reads output can pin the answer)
reading_rules.decode_rows: decode{s} is step s of the cached sequence, fed row s of the same generator draw AFTER the pinned prefill produced the state and window in prefill.state / prefill.conv_window; the decode rows are not independent of the prefill rows
